review: The Metro series has come a long way. The most immersive game series. Thank you for creating this wonderful universe and allowing us to truly feel the post-apocalyptic theme in our bones. Happy 15th Anniversary.

As the store page for the vanilla game is still available (i.e. the Redux edition does not make the original disappear) I am only going to concentrate on the new aspects of the game. Should you be interested in what Metro 2033 is about feel free to read my review on the vanilla game's store page.

Initially, I thought this Redux edition was only a graphical enhancement to the game released back in 2010. Make no mistake: the creators have done a superb job! Redux sports better lighting effects, more detailed textures and, to be honest, we have so many bits and pieces here that it is simply better to use YouTube and look for some comparison videos.

But is this good for us? Well, yes! Remember when Last Light came out? It offered better graphics so much so that we can say it was as Metro 2033 was originally intended to be. So, the developers picked this upgraded, more refined engine and remade all the levels of Metro 2033. We have the ultimate Metro 2033 experience now!

And the upgrades do not stop there: some new elements introduced in Last Light were also borrowed. For instance, melee was not possible but finally, taking out enemies silently is possible not just from the distance. Also, diary pages are now hidden throughout this game. Since you explored everything for the extra ammo now you can find these and read more about Artyom's thoughts and emotions.

Some sections were expanded upon and there are new sections such as the hall in Polis where you can stop by and marvel at the establishment along with the bartender who you can drink with. Beside the diary pages there are many safes hidden, as well. Keys to them appear on dead bodies or simply on shelves and while they glow in red due to the cobwebs sometimes it is difficult to spot them. Oh, cobwebs! We now have these and setting them on fire with the lighter is as fun as it was in Last Light!

Redux is the definitive version of Metro 2033. A version that expresses that this is how it should have been all along back in 2010. You can dismiss the idea if you want due to the fact that money is - once again - asked for it. However, if you are a true fan of Metro and you liked its sequel I'm sure it will be an immediate purchase for you. :)

Metro 2033 Redux is the vastly upgraded and improved version of the original Metro 2033 post-apocalyptic FPS game. First brought to gamers in 2010 by THQ and then given a complete makeover in 2014 by DeepSilver, the title is based off of the novel of the same name written by Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky. Though I have not personally read the book, friends of mine have stated that the game is very close to its origins, and the few differences are forgivable. 

First up, let's talk about the changes that the Redux brings. If you play, and/or own, the original Metro 2033, it's definitely worth your time and money to invest in this edition of the game. The updated graphics are a drastic improvement over the old title, bringing in high quality textures, dynamic lighting, and improved atmospheric effects such as fog, steam, and rain that bring an entirely new depth to the campaign. All of these changes combined make the darkened tunnels of the underground feel more claustrophobic, and the open areas more derelict. There have also been some alterations to a few of the major cutscenes; full side-by-side comparisons can be viewed on YouTube. On the other hand, there has also been notable outcry regarding the reduced difficulty of the overall experience, primarily when it comes to Survival mode, in that scavenged resources are more plentiful.

Now, if you haven't played Metro 2033 before, here's what it's all about: A nuclear war occurred in 2013, wherein Russia was targeted with atomic bombs that caused severe radiation; primarily across Moscow. The devastating impacts caused all survivors to flee into the underground tunnels of the metro stations, where they proceeded to build as much of new 'cities' as they could, each one being housed at a different base metro station, leaving the tunnels to connect them like roads. In the game, you play as a 20-year-old male survivor who was born prior to the nuclear fallout known as Artyom. The year is now 2033, and his home in the northern metro station, Exhibition, is under attack by a group of creatures that are referred to as the Dark ones. Artyom must travel to the main metro station of Polis and plead for help from their rangers to save his home, family, and friends.

Though Metro 2033 Redux is classified as a post-apocalyptic FPS title, it has deep survival elements to its gameplay. The currency of choice are military-grade bullets, which can be exchanged in a few metro stations for ammo, grenades, gas mask filters, med-kits,weapons, and weapon upgrades. The bullets themselves can be found by exploring every nook and cranny of the levels, and also from some scripted events that happen. Likewise, if you're unable to pony up the rounds for supplies, you can find all of the aforementioned things (sans weapon upgrades) by scavenging. However, playing on Survival mode, as opposed to the only other mode that the game has called Spartan, reduces the amount of supplies that you find out in the wild.

While enjoying your 10-13 hours of play time exploring the toxic, snowy wastelands and deep, dark corridors of tunnels, you will find that the game has a hefty arsenal of weaponry at your disposal; assault rifles, shotguns, revolvers, pneumatics, and even a flamethrower all make their appearances, plus a few others. The gun play is good, though the upgrades can be a bit lackluster, and you will find yourself shooting from the hip more often than not, as taking the time to aim can be futile since the enemies are incredibly speedy. It should also be mentioned that most of the guns are old-fashioned, and some of them, such as the flamethrower and pneumatics, require Super Soaker styled pumping to get them to work.

When it comes down to atmosphere, ambiance, graphics, and sound, THQ and DeepSilver thought of just about everything. From the thick fog, to green toxic air, rain that blurs your vision a little, spiders and flies that sometimes land on your gas mask, to downright having to wipe blood and grime off of your gas mask to see; the latter actually becomes rather prominent, as when you are in a heavy firefight, you will absolutely need to wipe the blood off to see where you're shooting. The soundtrack is just absolutely stunning, and as near to cinema quality as it can get. In fact, the entire game itself comes off as cinematic; at some point or another, it houses everything from horror, to action, to drama, to even fleeting moments of comedy.

Metro 2033 Redux can best be described as the lovechild of the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and Fallout series'. Though the levels are heavily enclosed in most cases, there's almost always a ton of chambers, decrepit buildings, and passages to explore. There's also a high level of replayability, as there are two different modes and two different endings to obtain; along with 51 worthwhile diary entries to pick up and read. It's worth standing around and listening to the conversations that people around you are having, as you can gain more insight into the story and it's also really immersing. Everything about this title is as near-perfect as a video game can get, and that means that it most definitely needs to be in your library at some point.

[h1][b]Storyline: [/b][/h1]
The game is set 20 years after a nuclear holocaust that takes place in Russia. Moscow has devolved into a ruined wasteland populated by bloodthirsty mutants and the toxic air has rendered the terrain uninhabitable. The Metro tunnels are the only remaining option for the survivors. Since new creatures known as the Dark Ones have the capacity to influence people's minds, you, Artyom, are determined to eliminate the threat to humanity. Will you be able to save your fellow survivors or will their already dismal life come to an end? Play the game to find out!

The game's story, in my opinion, is quite interesting and compelling. The game's entire tone is dark, and the story is pretty fitting. The game lasts approximately 8-9 hours.

[h1][b]🎮Gameplay:[/b][/h1]
The Metro series is well known for its premise and the concept of 'searching your surroundings' for ammo and basic survival item. I mean, the game is set in a world where creatures have taken control of the surface, so collecting every bullet you find while traversing the Metro's terrifying tunnels is crucial for your survival. When vital survival equipment is scarce, mankind will naturally battle one another. As a result, you come across both humans and animals who are ready to kill you at first sight. The gameplay is filled with stealth, combat, and horror. There is no such thing as a safe spot; any bloodthirsty mutant could attack you at any time, or you could just perish from the toxic gas owing to a lack of filters.

[b]Combat: [/b]
Humans will always find a way to kill each other, even if weaponry is limited. So, there is diverse gear available for both playstyles, such as throwing knives for a stealth approach and explosives for a guns-blazing approach. Of course, there are numerous weapons to pick from in the game, all of which may be fully customized. I know that going guns-blazing is much more fun than sneaking through the enemies, however, there are two endings in the game, so your actions throughout the game will determine which one you’ll get. So, think twice before you kill someone!

[b]Environment: [/b]
The game is designed to depict a world where creatures rule and everything created by humans is in ruins. But does it actually showcase what it intends to show to the players? The answer is yes! It truly feels like you're battling for your life in a world littered with the bodies of unfortunate individuals and ruined structures, as well as human stations populated by melancholy people who frequently narrate stories about the surface. Just wait until you play the "Depository" mission. It's the game's scariest mission, and you'll find out why if you play it.

[b]AI and Difficulty: [/b] 
As a huge fan of the series, I completed the game on three difficulties. In every difficulty, the mutant AI is nearly identical; the only variable is the amount of damage you incur on higher difficulties. The behavior of human enemies, on the other hand, is noticeably different. On higher levels, they'll readily recognize you, making completing the game discreetly a misery. On higher levels, even the most basic HUD features and hints are missing, and the worst part is that you can't see how much ammo you have in your current clip. So, if this is your first time playing the game, stick to the Normal or Hardcore difficulties and avoid the Ranger modes!

[h1][b]📷Graphics:[/b][/h1]
The game looks decent if you can manage to run it on max settings, but if you have a low rig, then the game will look a bit outdated. But trust me, the amount of fun you’ll have while playing the game is surely worth the sacrifice. For those who can run it at max settings, there will undoubtedly be many screenshot-worthy moments as you explore the destroyed Metro tunnels. I did face some visual bugs while playing the game, but they were minor bugs and can be overlooked. The only bothersome bug worth mentioning is that you can get stuck in certain areas and have to restart the game from the latest checkpoint in order to progress. It's a pain, but I've only had it twice.

[h1][b]🏷️Tips to new players:[/b][/h1] 
Don't rush through the game and take your time exploring the area. If you try to finish it quickly, you will run out of ammo and the game will become unplayable. Also, for human enemies, use assault rifles, and keep a shotgun on hand for mutants, as shotguns are far more effective against them.

[h1][b]😇Honest Rating:[/b][/h1]
If you're seeking for a horror-themed first-person shooter, don't wait any longer and purchase the game. Although twenty dollars for a single-player game is a bit excessive, I would strongly advise purchasing it during a sale.

Metro 2033 is an incredibly atmospheric and fun game that will immerse you and with Exodus coming I just had to make this review!

[h1] GAMEPLAY [/h1]
     The gameplay in this game is fantastic, with the gas mask and flashlight mechanics, this game will totally immerse you in the atmosphere of the Metro universe. The transition between levels makes sense and the progression of Artyom's gear is also well done. Listening in on citizens of the Metro conversing with one another is very fun, and sad at times too!

     The combat in this game is intense, especially on Hardcore and Ranger mode, trading shots while wiping your mask make the combat in this game a treat and feel great, the enemies and weapons in the game are varied as well, from the lowly bandit to the heavily armored soldier. The stealth sections are great and allow replayability for the game as there are different endings depending on your actions through out the game!

       The only thing I don't really like is that Artyom is a silent protagonist, if he can talk in the loading screen why can't he talk in the actual game, as alot of characters who talk to him seem like they're talking to themselves, that and the AI can be a bit silly at times, nothing too bad though.

[h1] STORY [/h1]
     The story in this game is very interesting and will hold your attention as you follow the same person from the novel Artyom Alekseyevich Chyornyj, the game offers many memorible characters, you'll recognize them when you see them! The voice acting is very well done as well as the story telling in the game, through Artyom's journals.

[h1] AUDIO AND MUSIC [/h1]
     The sounds design in this game is amazing, from mutant screams to the blast of a quad-barreled shotgun, the guns in this game feel real in their sounds and the sound track is great and fits the game very well. The small sound of water droplets and wind, further the immersion of this game.

[h1] GRAPHICS [/h1]
     The attention to detail in the game was very good, definately a step up from the original. The lighting in the game, that with the overall art design make the game look beautiful, the game was for sure ahead of most games at the time! Though there were a few "flickering" terrain bugs, there is also a lack of options to customize your graphics settings..

[h1] OVERALL [/h1]
     Small problems aside, Metro 2033 REDUX is a great game, and is definitly worth it's asking price. All in all this game gets an [h1] 8/10 [/h1] A great game with a few tiny problems, that won't interfere with your experience!

이 외의 전투시 적 등장숫자나 받는 데미지 입히는 데미지, UI표기여부 등은 전부 하위분류 난이도(노멀~레인저 등)에 따라 차이가 날 뿐입니다. 개인적으론 굳이 이런식으로 나눠서 도전과제 때문에 2회차를 강제하는 게 썩 마음에 들지는 않았습니다.

쉬워진 잠입플레이 - 기존 은신 시스템과 달리 시계 불이 들어오고 안들어오고 2가지로 바뀌었고 은신복/대형아머 등의 요소도 사라져 은신플레이가 훨 쉬워졌습니다. 광원이 닿는 곳만 아니라면 적의 코앞에 가만히 있기만 해도 발각되지 않으며 오리지널에 비해 발각범위가 현저하게 감소해 웬만한 거리에서 뛰어다녀도 적들의 의심을 사지 않습니다. 시시해짐과 동시에 간편해져 좋은 점도 있습니다.

게임전반의 시스템 및 UI변경 - 기존의 메트로 라스트 라이트처럼 총알 갯수 제한, 총기 종류별로 1정씩 3정 보유하던 것에서 종류무관 3정(레인저는 2정)으로 변경, 수류탄 투척방식 변경, 단검 투척방식 변경, 거래 방식 변경, 총기 커스터마이징 추가 등이 있습니다.

총평 - 기존작을 억지로 했던 유저가 아니라면 메트로 라스트라이트 리덕스와는 달리 2033 리덕스는 꼭 한 번 해볼만 합니다. 생각보다 바뀐 점을 많이 발견할 수 있으며, 그런것들을 찾아보는 재미도 쏠쏠합니다. 다만 메트로 라스트라이트는 광원효과 말고는 상술된 요소중에 바뀐 점이 하나도 없으니 참고하시길.

2033 has the best atmosphere by a MILE.

from dark, cold n empty moscow to stations of fire, laughter n водка.

the sound engine was developed specifically for 2033 and it shows. i have not once in 100s of games heard a game sound so accurate, so real and overwhelming, gunshots recorded in ukranian underground tunnels, footsteps perfectly matching spatial perception. 2014 graphics become irrelevant when you understand how well the atmosphere and sound synergise.

the combat is nothing special in all honesty, basic 1st person shooter although decent weapon choice and customisation, but the story is where this game really shines.

the world is ending, theres only room for survival, the game forces you to choose between morals yet gives you the option to choose the type of person you want to be. the future seems overwhelmingly bleak, yet you can still find moments of laughter, drinking and reminiscing with your fellow russian comrades. 

its not just the story thats bleak, its the pressure the game constantly puts you under, reminding you that you're in a time of scarcity, every bullet is a choice – spend it on an enemy or save it to buy filters for your gas mask, either way, you're always running out of something.

as a polish man i dont think 4A games could have executed the eastern european / soviet atmosphere any better than they did, if your slavic you will appreciate this game more than most.

played at 1440p low settings 60-120fps consistently on a 27 inch monitor, powered by rog ally, zero stuttering or performance issues.

flawless execution of a concept, even if not 100% polished. 9.6/10.

I played through the original Metro 2033 back in August of 2014 and I absolutely loved it. However, I personally purchased Metro 2033 Redux for some easy achievements and a what once was an extremely rare badge. That's not to say that I didn't enjoy what I experienced, but I feel there's a lot to praise and criticize 4A Games on with this product.

[h1][b]Let's start off with the major additions to Metro 2033 Redux mentioned in trailers, shall we?[/b][/h1]

● The ability to wipe your mask. Just as in Metro: Last Light, you can now wipe your mask as many times as you like! Don't forget to wipe it 20 times when you first start the game for an easy achievement!

● Plenty of new locations to discover in each chapter. These locations consist of military grade ammunition, dirary pages, and keys to safes that contain a considerable amount of resources.

● Arytom's Diary pages to find and collect. You're probably thinking "Oh great, more things to collect!" but if you're anything like me, you like to learn everything you can about the products you purchase.

● Enhanced weather, lighting and ecosystem. This time around Metro 2033 Redux is much brighter, has creatures as in Metro: Last Light and throughout the game has changes in weather. The creatures consist of spiders, baby shrimp and what I believe to be mutated birds.

[h1][b][u]Features of Metro 2033 Redux worth praising:[/u][/b][/h1]

● The ability to approach a combat situation in multiple ways. Sneaking, knock out kills, use of silencers, and using the darkness to sneak up on enemies. It may seem silly and common knowledge but many games in the current gaming industry fail to deliver anything more than just a watered down run and gun experience.

● The A.I. combat subroutines are irritating yet innovative. If you're approaching a combat situation guns blazing be prepard for some jumpy, trigger happy enemies.

● The kills saving system. In the original Metro 2033 kills were only saved in a consecutive playthrough. This time around, you can reload checkpoints to accumulate kills for revolvers, shotguns, assault rifles, pneumatic weapons, etc.

● No unsynced voice and facial animations. Although a little wonky, the facial animations and voice are never unsynced from start to finish. That's certainly saying something considering the majority of the games created today have the issue with unsynced facial animations.

● No 'in-game' store. The majority of developers feel the need to put a direct link to their game's downloadable content within the game itself. This angers some consumers while ruining the immersion they're trying to create.

[h1][b][u]Aspects of Metro 2033 Redux worth criticizing:[/u][/b][/h1]

● The so called "seamless" transition between chapters always isn't as smooth as they've lead you to believe. As I played through 2033 Redux I recall 4A Games tying at least 3 chapters together. In the chapter Driving to Sparta the screen goes black at one point and you're teleported to the above ground ranger base.

● The retexturing of the majority of NPCs within the game. While they may have retextured many of the non-player characters within the game, that certianly does not mean they did it for the better. In some cases, the animations look signifigantly worse than the original Metro 2033. Personally, I would rather have a higher resolution, more detailed NPC than a completely different version of one.

● Non-existant NPC eye tracking. I never realized how important eye tracking was before I played the Metro series. All of the NPCs in Metro 2033 Redux feel as if they're staring off into space, unaware of their surroundings or the player.

● Copy and paste menus and user interface. The menu and user interface of Metro 2033 Redux is the exact menu and user interface that Metro: Last Light used back in 2013. 


Overall, I enjoyed this game and would absolutely recommend it if the price is right.

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Metro 2033[/b] is a post-apocalyptic FPS heavily focusing on narrative, survival aspects, and is developed by [i]4A Games[/i]. Inspired to Dimitry Glukhovsky's three-book long novel "Metro", this game is set in Soviet Russia after the Cold War went wrong, annihilating most of humanity with nuclear weapons. The title [b]narrates the story of Artyom[/b], at first just another of the numerous apocalypse survivors, soon enough to be [b]involved into a series of events that will decide the fate of the whole Metro and his own.[/b]

There are many valid reasons this title is [b]rightly considered a masterpiece of the adventure-FPS genre[/b]: first of all, [b]the exceptional setting delivers a fresh believable take on the post-apocalyptic genre[/b], showing off the brutal reality nuclear holocaust survivors have to endure. With superb graphics, this title [b]sports some of the best visuals, effects and environments ever seen in gaming history[/b], with very few other games coming even close. Secondly, Metro also [b]builds a perfectly paced, varied, and extremely involving gameplay experience[/b] composed at the core of plentiful action segments, resource management, meaningful exploration full of secrets, while also mini-games, on-rail sections on vehicles, even chase sequences thrown into the mix - [b]and manages to do all of it almost flawlessly[/b], with very few marginal problems. Last but not least, [b]the presence of many difficulty levels ensures all kinds of players can enjoy this experience[/b], from a Story-oriented easy mode to the brutally difficult Ranger Hardcore setting.

The [b]only problem worth mentioning[/b] with Metro is the [b]presence of quick-time events during several cut-scenes[/b], failure in performing them means death, [b]this is an issue especially on Ranger Hardcore difficulty where all HUD is removed, including the prompts telling you which button to press[/b] - "E" most of the time - not really a smart design choice. For the rest, I really have [b]nothing else negative to say which is extremely rare[/b] - attesting even more so that this game is some of the finest, best-crafted, finely polished experiences out there.

Overall [b]Metro 2033[/b] is [b]a real masterpiece for this genre, excelling in all fields and delivering a level of gameplay, design, graphics, storytelling and immersion very few other games could rival[/b]. Currently [b]priced at 20€[/b] in its "Redux" version, which is the same as the normal game just with even better graphics, and [b]offering about 8-10 hours of gameplay depending on difficulty and exploration ratio, I can definitely suggest getting this game at full price to anyone[/b], save for those who really can't stomach FPS or post-apocalyptic settings - for all other players, a sure-fire purchase.

[h1]Pros & Cons[/h1]

🔵 [b]Pros[/b]
+ Exceptional graphics, ensuring a high level of immersion at all times, spectacular action and impressive landscapes.
+ Superb combat featuring realistic gun feel, solid challenge on high difficulties, varied approaches from stealth to action.
+ Meaningful exploration filled with secrets, additional areas, critical to find on high difficulties to not run out of supplies.
+ Varied gameplay situations featuring on-rail vehicle segments, chase sequences, stealth and mini-games.
+ Resource management mechanics, united with shops and scarce loot in general, give much more depth compared to a "normal" FPS gameplay.

🔴 [b]Cons[/b]
- Quick time events are annoying especially on Ranger difficulty where HUD is removed. 
- The game ends. But don't worry, Last Light and Exodus got you covered.


[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]

🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
The gameplay of Metro 2033 is divided into Exploration, Character Management, Mini-games and Combat.

[b]Exploration[/b] in actually the main activity in Metro, more so than combat: crossing the frozen wastes of the surface, or the dark tunnels underground, players will find themselves going through a variety of environments mostly on foot, where a keen eye for secondary areas and loot are essential. With superb environments and graphics, exploring every new area is an experience best taken slowly, not only to find most secrets and loot which is important, but also to savor the atmosphere. While on "regular" difficulties HUD and some hints will help you finding loot, where to go more easily, the Ranger difficulty, which delivers the "true" Metro experience, removed HUD completely, delivering a realism level very few games dare having. Safes unlocked with keys found in other places, rooms, sometimes whole buildings can be areas off the beaten path, containing not just supplies but even scorches of lore to expend your knowledge.

[b]Character Management[/b] is all about resource conservation: with limits to every type of bullets, consumables and medkits you can carry, making every shot count, healing when really necessary and making a run for it when needs be are all things to take into account, as said before, looting every possible resource is fundamental. In peaceful stations, players can sell unused bullets for military grade ammo which doubles as currency, in order to buy new weapons, modify existing ones, or replenish supplies - everything comes at high prices though, only the most conservative players will be able to afford the priciest weapons and modifications before late-game. In contaminated areas, keeping an eye on remaining filters for your mask, and its integrity, are also added mechanics to keep up pressure. 

[b]Mini-games[/b] can be found at some stations and mainly consist in shooting galleries of increasing difficulty, awarding prizes in Military Bullets if completed - needless to say, very worth doing. I also am prone to consider on-rail sections, where for example you man a stationary gun, as mini games of sorts, as health / damage resistances of the character are different and some things are also scripted to happen.

[b]Combat[/b] is perhaps the best aspect of Metro, delivering an uncompromising, realistic system where a few shots can kill both yourself and most enemies. Ammo is generally scarce, grenades and high caliber guns instantly kill pretty much always, while the enemy at least on Ranger, employs good tactics, uses cover and generally puts up a good fight also for superior numbers. Stealth or loud, which are both completely viable at all difficulties, Metro's combat delivers excellent gun feeling, realism, and brutality, as it should be. War is hell after all, and Metro knows this perfectly.

🔩 [b]Performance Analysis[/b]
[u]PC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4[/u]
There are no technical problems impairing performance or stability - but of course given the game's impressive graphics, even today in 2019 only medium-high and high-end machines will be able to run this game well, especially on 1440p resolutions. On this config, achieving 144fps in 1440p maxed out was possible with 2X AA (4X AA resulted in 40-45 FPS, damn son!) and not at all times, generally more about 70-95 FPS. This extreme requirement is justified however by the graphics it delivers - it's another Crysis, pretty much.

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
[b]Metro 2033[/b] is a masterpiece of gaming, excelling in all fields and delivering an experience so good any self-respecting gaming enthusiast should run through at least once in their lives.

Metro 2033 Redux is the remaster of the first Metro game, released alongside a Last Light remaster.

Story:

You play as Artyom. After a nuclear war devastates the earth everyone is forced to live in the underground metro tunnels to avoid the radiation left by the bombs. One day the station Artyom lives in is attacked by a race called the Dark Ones and after the attack he's sent out to look for help in the other parts of the metro against the Dark Ones.

The story of Metro 2033 is dark, moody and just absolutely awesome. It's often told in scraps like listening to people talk about the old days and other stuff that had happened after the bombs fell. Artyom also has a few things to say before each level and his writings are usually pretty interesting and add quite a bit depth to the already lore heavy story.

Graphics:

Metro 2033 was already a brilliant looking game and I think it aged really well, so when I originally heard they were remastering it I was confused, but after seeing the new version in action I will say that a lot of the changes are decent, albeit some people might not like them. One of the major things is the colors are much more intense in the Redux version.

The original version of the game often had muted colors and it helped build this world that has died due to the bombs and that continued after even stepping outside of the metro tunnels. The new version feels a lot more alive, which does somewhat kill the apocalyptic look the original went with, but to an extent I did enjoy it. 

Everything looks about on par with the original just higher resolution, but there were quite a few character models that I noticed that weren't in the main game. Upon digging (and more on this later) this redux version has a lot of the assets pulled from the Last Light version of the game and even some new sections built with those assets.

Audio:

I will first mention what I absolutely adore about the game and that's the atmosphere ambience, gun sounds and the music. The ambience helps build and absolutely amazing atmosphere that sticks with you. You're going through these massive metro tunnels with bad guys and mutants possibly lurking behind every possible turn, giving you chills, even more so later on when you get outside. 

The music is also really good, I love it especially when you visit a station and see people sitting near a fire singing and playing music on guitars it's just really awesome stuff. Gun and most of your equipment just sounds absolutely on point, so they definitely nailed that aspect. 

As for the voice acting, I've seen many people say they like and for the most part it is decent, but I'll admit that a lot of is just really cheesy and does kill quite a few moments. Not to say all of it is bad, which is definitely not, but I will admit that there's quite a few characters that sounds really stupid. 

Gameplay:

Metro 2033 Redux is a first person shooter, with light stealth elements. Metro 2033 is a very linear game where you often go through corridors of enemies trying to go from A to B. You take on enemies with an assortment of weaponry, but one of the big things of Metro is how ammo is not always going to be something you have plenty off so you will have to be careful on when you pick a fight. 

You can often scrounge up ammo from dead bodies and in rare instances you can find something called Military grade ammo, which is the rarest type of ammo and is used in the game as currency for upgrades and other items, or if you're out it can be used as actual ammo which does extra damage, but it's best to try to keep it until you reach a merchant. 

The shooting feels fine, even though it does get incredibly janky at times. The janky combat mostly likes to act up when you get swarmed with tons of enemies, but not as much when you're in stealth. Stealth is pretty basic as in you crouch down and remain out of sight. I didn't like stealth all that much since often I felt like I was seen from places where I simply couldn't have been seen from which is incredibly disappointing. 

Now one of the biggest changes is that the game is remastered to match closer to Last Light. Most of the stuff is entirely changed from the original version and to some these changes could make the game worse to play, but overall I didn't mind these changes whatsoever and actually appreciated the game slightly more. 

Verdict:

As far as remasters goes, this is one is about the least offensives ones released. I liked all the changes and playing the game again with these slight upgrades was a blast. If you haven't played 2033 before this is a great way to play the game and honestly I have no trouble recommending this.

Final Rating:
9/10

Metro 2033 Redux is a remastered version of Metro 2033, made in the engine of its sequel, Metro: Last Light. To begin with, the engine upgrade brings some graphical enhancements like better character models and environments, making the game look a lot better. However, that's not all, it also brings some gameplay changes, as well as new collectibles in the form of diaries, which give further details about the story.

The story is based on the book Metro 2033, by Dmitry Glukhovsky, set in a post-apocalyptic Moscow, after a nuclear war in 2013 forced everyone in the city to take shelter within its Metro system. Because of the high amount of radiation that was released in the atmosphere, animals (and those humans who were unlucky enough to not reach the safety of the Metro) became mutants. The player takes the role of Artyom, a young man living in Exhibition station, who must embark on a mission for help after the Dark Ones, mutated humans who live on the surface, begin attacking his home station.

Something I like about the story and the setting, is that it's not your typical post-apocalyptic game, in which the nukes fell and mutants came to be. There's also a certain supernatural element to the game, as there's a few events that can't be simply explained as a result of the radiation. That's not something you see a lot in games with this setting. Plus, the fact that it takes place (mostly) within a Metro system gives it a higher degree of creepyness, as you're locked in these dark tunnels, and the monsters could come from anywhere.

The gameplay is that of a typical FPS; while there is some room for exploration, most levels are relatively linear; in fact, in all cases you're always heading from point A to point B, perhaps having to do something before moving on. Artyom can carry up to three guns, which can be upgraded at stores, plus four different throwable objects (knives and different types of grenades). He also carries a gas mask, which is necessary to cross some areas in which the air is toxic, so you might have to spend some time exploring in order to find filters for your mask, as the air it provides is limited.

The game also includes a Moral Points system. Depending on your actions, you can earn or lose these points, and getting a certain amount of them (which the game never specifies) allows you to get a good ending. These points are usually rewarded for exploration, or for taking more time to learn from the game world; a pretty good system in my opinion, and the fact that it's ambiguos to an extent is pretty interesting. There's also the fact that there's special ammo, the Military Grade Rounds, which are also used as currency, meaning that if you decided to use it, you'd be literally shooting your money.

As for difficulty, well, the game includes two main gameplay modes: Spartan, which is more action oriented (and somewhat reminiscent of Last Light's regular gameplay), and Survival, which is closer to the original Metro 2033's gameplay. Then there's also the option between regular and ranger mode; in ranger mode some HUD elements are removed, and the combat is a bit more challenging, as weapons are deadlier.

The environments are great. It really gives the sense of a post-apocalyptic Moscow, both in indoor environments, like when you're in the Metro, as well as outdoor ones, when you come to the surface. The "Dead City" as its called in the game, feels like both a calm and terrible place, giving you a sense of discomfort as you move through it. And the claustrophobic tunnels of the Metro might keep you on your nerves, as you try to make your way through its darkness.

Personally, I'm a big fan of the Metro series. I recommend this game.

[h1]INTRODUCTION:[/h1]
Metro 2033 Redux is the ‘remastered’ version of Metro 2033 which was originally released in 2010. The game is a first-person horror survival shooter based on a novel of the same title written by Dmitry Glukhovsky and serves as the first title of the franchise. 

The 2014 Redux version contains the graphical and gameplay changes from Metro: Last Light.

[h1]PLOT (No Spoilers):[/h1]
The player takes on the role of Artyom (Артём), a young man who has lived his entire life within the confines of his home Metro Station below Moscow. Join him as he is set on a quest to save it from a new threat that may potentially wipe out the remnants of humanity who survived the nuclear apocalypse.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
+ Great atmosphere and world design;
+ Very good graphics but…(see CON #1 and #2)
+ Very good sound design and voice acting;
+ Surprising level variety despite being stuck mostly in a metro (subway) system;
+ Magnificent graphics and excellent use of PhysX technology;
+ Good story that offers alternate endings and a very subtle morality system that does affect the outcome of the game;
+ Great blend of action, horror and suspense;
+ Challenging difficulty;
+ Weapon variety with an upgrade system;
+ Linear story backed up by substantial story driven content;
+ Refreshing new setting of Russia; and
+ Lengthy game time.

[h1]CONS:[/h1]

- Very low default field of view (FOV); [b][u][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=306901616]FIX[/url][/u][/b];
- Long and unskippable intro before reaching the main screen; and
- Removed the ability of the player to purchase armor/outfit based on playstyle.

[h1]NEUTRAL:[/h1]

[h1]CONCLUSION:[/h1]
[b]GREAT GAME.[/b] Metro 2033 delivers a unique and very immersive first person shooter experience. It blends together the atmosphere of narrative driven games, the suspense of horror games, and the heart pumping combat of action games.

[b]Who am I:[/b]

Hi there! My name is Claire, I am 26 years old and from Denmark. I have over 20 years of gaming experience. I do all achievements for the game before I review it. So my review truly reflects a 100% completion of the game.
Eventhough my reviews are quite long and extensive, I try my very best to keep them as spoiler free as possible.
Remember to take everything I say with a grain of salt, as it is just my subjective opinion. Hope you enjoy! :3

[b]Gameplay:[/b]

Metro 2033 Redux falls into the genre we know as a modern First-Person-Shooter. You play through a linear world where you interact and experience whatever the game sets out to show you. There is very little exploration and alternative paths to take. Thus it is more akin to games such as Call of Duty, rather than oldschool FPS' such as Doom or Duke Nukem.

The lack of player exploration allows the game developers to create some truly awe-shocking and atmospheric moments, both through it's gameplay but also its story. This is in my opinion Metros strongest quality, and will be further expanded on in the Story section.

It is clear that Metro 2033 Redux wants the player to truly feel immersed in the gameworld. This is very evident if you look at how the game handles its game mechanics. 

When you enter the post-apocalyptic Moscow you have to wear your gasmask because the air is toxic. You, as the player, have to manually put your gas mask on. You also have to monitor your gas mask filter on your watch. Once your filter is running low, you have to equip a new one, or you will simply die.

The same goes with your flashlight. You want your flashlight turned on almost all of the time because the game is very dark, especially in the deep abandoned places of the Metro. However your flashlight has to be charged by the player manually, by taking out a DIY charger and pumping a new charge into the flashlight.

There are many instances of this mechanic in Metro 2033 Redux, and I thoroughly enjoyed it a lot. It not only makes you much more engaged in the gameplay, but it also adds a clever level of fear as your flashlight potentially runs out of power while being chased by monsters. 

Throughout your time in the Metro you will encounter a variety of weapons to play with. All of the weapons feel distinct from one another, with the exception of a few of the assault rifles which in my opinion didn't have much of a different feel to them. You are able to customize your weapons with different scopes and handles etc. I feel that this was not expanded on well enough. There simply was not enough upgrades for it to feel very meaningful.

Metro 2033 Redux has a TON of stealth sections. Atleast if you play them "the way it's intended" because you are able to run and gun your way through all stealth sections of the game. The AI in Metro 2033 Redux is probably the worst AI I have seen in many years. You are able to literally walk right past NPC's that seem to be looking directly at you. Yet on the other hand if you end up getting spotted by just one person, the whole area suddenly knows where you are and will hunt you down until you either die or kill everyone in the area.

I wanted to stealth my way through the game, so when I got spotted I had to restart to the last checkpoint as there was no way for me to reset my "stealth". This felt gimmicky and is not the way you want your stealth gameplay to work. 

It took me 9 hours to complete the game on Survival mode, and only 7 hours on Spartan mode. I would recommend Survival mode.

[b]Story:[/b]

You play as Artyom, a young man from one of the Northern Metro stations. Your station has been under attack by the mysterious "Dark Ones" for a while, and your station needs help. You set out on your way to the capital of the Metro called Polis to help your station. On your long road through the Metros web of stations you will encounter many different people and maybe more disturbingly... Many different monsters.

I don't want to spoil anymore than that, as the story is truly one of the selling points of Metro 2033 Redux. The whole game is  built up around a best-selling novel called Metro 2033 by Dmitry Glukhovsky.

While the game is very linear it makes sure to give you a lot of dialogue that helps you understand the world you're in. I feel like they could've easily elaborated on the story a lot more. Although there is an expansion called Metro Last Light which I haven't played, which supposedly expands on the whole Metro universe.

[b]Graphics:[/b]

While the game is a few years old now, it still has absolutely jaw-dropping graphics. The polygon-counts may not be the highest we have ever seen in a game, but Metro 2033 Redux has something most games desperately wants. It has soul in its graphical fidelity. By that I mean the metro stations looks run down. The people in the metros look ragged and dirty. The weapons look home-made, which most of them are. The disfigured faces and dismembered bodies of the people who died on the surface frightens the player of what to come.

I always felt that no matter where I looked in Metro 2033 Redux I would be looking at a convincing piece of a post-apolyptic world. I never lost my sense of immersion, because everything seemed just right for the world I had been placed in. 

The lighting effects in Metro 2033 Redux is some of the best lighting effects I have ever seen. A lot of care and detail went into the lighting effects and it is a clever decision, because you spend most of the game in very dark areas where you can really show off some amazing lighting effects. The game even goes so far as to use this lighting mechanic when you fight some of the monsters in the Metro.

With that being said the facial animations of some, if not most of the humans in the game are not very good. They don't look very convincing in my opinion, but I think it boils down to the game being a few years old. I actually found some of the human faces much more scary than the monsters. :P

[b]Sound:[/b]

The background music of Metro 2033 Redux is okay. I didn't feel like it was anything special, and I didn't stop and listen at any point in time. I think this was intentional by the game developers. They didn't want big musical scores booming in the background. They wanted their music to compliment their two strongest factors of the game. The story telling and the atmospheric immersion. If this was their intention, I think they hit it spot on. 

The game uses sound to communicate to the player if they are about to be spotted during stealth sections. This is nothing new, but it works quite well in Metro 2033.

The gun sounds are okay without being anything special.
The sounds of the monsters range from okay to very good. The very good sounds from the monsters were the skittering of spiders crawling into holes behind you, or the distant howl of a Nosalis (A big mutant creature). These sounds were very useful to the game, as they helped to create tension and immersion.

I played the game with the english voices, and the voice-acting in Metro 2033 Redux is not that great. It is acceptable without being good. It is not bad enough to be a problem though, with the exception of the kids voice acting, which is just downright strange in my opinion.

[b]Price:[/b]

You can buy Metro 2033 for 19.99€ or your regional equivalent. You can buy it as a bundle with Metro Last Light. 
It frequently goes on sale on Steam, and I would recommend you to wait for a steam discount before purchasing.

[b]Conclusion:[/b]

Metro 2033 Redux is a very atmospheric and immersive FPS game set in a post-apocalyptic world. It has average gunplay with some clever added mechanics through the management of gas masks, filters and your flashlight.
It has a great story with two different endings.

If you even remotely enjoy linear and story driven FPS games you should give Metro 2033 Redux a chance.

I give Metro 2033 Redux 8 out of 10.

Metro 2033 Redux is a hauntingly atmospheric first person shooter that pulls you deep into its bleak, post apocalyptic vision of Moscow. Based on Dmitry Glukhovsky’s novel, the game follows Artyom, a young survivor who has lived his entire life in the metro tunnels after a nuclear war rendered the surface uninhabitable. When his home station is threatened by mysterious creatures known as the Dark Ones, Artyom embarks on a perilous journey through the ruined metro system to reach Polis, seeking help from other factions and uncovering unsettling truths about humanity’s survival. The story is linear but tightly written, and what makes it stand out is its focus on tone and atmosphere over spectacle. It’s not about constant firefights it’s about tension, scarcity, and the quiet dread of surviving underground. Conversations overheard in stations, flickering lights, gas mask filters running low all of these details create a tangible sense of place. Metro 2033 Redux has an insane level of immersion, the sound design is amazing, and some of the best atmospheric storytelling. The muffled echoes in the tunnels, the oppressive darkness, and the subtle use of environmental storytelling all contribute to what many consider one of the most immersive single player shooters ever made. Do yourself a favour and play with Russian audio with English subs and it becomes so much more immersive, for me at least but worth a try. 

That said, not everyone will love its pacing. Some find it too slow, too methodical, or frustratingly punishing  especially on higher difficulties where ammo and filters are scarce(I believe this is how the game was meant to be played, and is the most conducive to how the original felt and played.) But for players who appreciate deliberate tension over nonstop gunfights, that’s exactly what makes Metro 2033 so special. The Redux version  isn’t just a remaster it’s the definitive way to experience one of the most atmospheric and emotionally grounded shooters of its generation. It’s not for everyone, but if you enjoy focused, immersive narrative shooters that make you feel every step through the darkness, this one is absolutely worth playing.

The survival horror genre has started a number of recognizable gameplay traditions. The constant tension, the emphasis on atmosphere, the helplessness of the main character, limited items/ammo -- all of these mechanics are among the reasons why survival horror games are so enticing. Metro 2033 is a first-person shooter that borrows heavily from these traditions in order to create an atmospheric experience. Although Metro 2033 is an intriguing journey, I was terribly frustrated by a number of stealth scenarios and technical glitches.

Based on a Russian novel by Dmitry Glukhovsky, Metro 2033 is set in post-apocalyptic Moscow. After nuclear devastation ravaged the earth and skies, the people of Moscow retreated into the sprawling underground Metro system in order to survive, building tattered towns at various stations throughout. The world is populated by mutants, dangerous anomalies and a number of supernatural occurrences. In the midst of this strange setting, players take control of the young Artyom and guide him on his quest to deliver an important message to a neighboring station. He'll fight a ton of generic enemies in order to get there, with a few surprises along the way.

Metro 2033 was definitely showing its age by the time the redux came out. I don't have the original on steam, just on console. It most likely looks much better on pc. 

The Redux isn't just another "HD Retexture" of  2033; it is a complete rebuild of it on the Metro:LL engine. The enhancements made are obvious when you first boot up the game, but I'll do my best to break it down.

Graphics:

Compared to the orignal's graphics, this is a no contest. The skyboxes are better, the lighting is better, and the textures are better. I think there were a few textures that looked a bit low resolution, but it wasn't a bother. Overall, they more than hold their own against other recent games. 8.5/10

Sound:

The sounds in Metro Redux are excellent. Everything from ambient noise to the combat sounds were spot on. The ambient noise constantly kept me on edge, and did a great job in adding to the immersion. Personally, I think this is the strongest aspect of the game. 10/10

Story: 

To avoid giving away spoilers, I'm going to keep this brief. It doesn't exactly follow the book, but it is still good, and believable in the context of the game. 8.5/10

AI:

Probably the worst part of the game. The AI is pretty bad, especially the friendly AI. It will not see enemies even when they are right in front of it, The enemy AI is also disappointing. It seems to ignore obvious signs of the player's presence, and has poor detection capabilities. Once combat starts, it still appears to have trouble finding good ways to engage the player. It blindly runs out of cover, straight into your line of fire, or ends up getting stuck in a neat single-file line as it approaches from a distance. However, it does have its moments, and can put up a serious challenge, especially at higher difficulties. 6.5/10

Overall, this game is solid, and well worth the money. If you enjoyed the original, I think you will enjoy this.

Metro 2033, based on the Novel  with the same name from Dmitri Alexejewitsch Gluchowski, and takes part in the underground Metro-Network of Moscow in the fallout of a Nuclear war. 
The survivors who could fled into the underground when the bombs fell developed a society over the years. Each Metro station became like a Village on its own, with its own rules and purpose within the Metro. But. as we humans are, over time several factions emerged from the survivors and started to fight each other over resources and territory, while mutants roaming the surface in the ruins of Moscow. But these aren’t the only dangers that wait for you within the vast tunnels of the Metro. 
You take the role of Artyom, a young man living in one of the outer stations. You have a simple goal; you look for someone and you have to deliver a message to one of the most central stations…
    
I’m so glad I finally got around to play this game. The story is great, the gunplay is fine and the weapon upgrade systems feels meaningful. What really give the gunfights more weight than it does in other games is, that your bullets are also the currency within the Metro, so you really want to be careful and not to trigger-happy whenever possible. This gives the fights a whole different dynamic than it does in other shooters.  
But most of all, the atmosphere. That is where Metro 2033 really succeeds. The tunnels feel claustrophobic at times, it’s dark, so you often have to rely on your headlamp, everywhere is decay and plants taking over. The world feels alive…and somewhat real. 
And even in the stations where things are in order, as far as that is possible, you see the despair in people everywhere. The living quarters, public spaces, markets, hospitals. Everything looks like it had been built from the things that were found and somehow held together.    
I haven’t played a game that was this immersive in a long time. 

If you, like me, haven’t got around to play Metro 2033 yet, you absolutely should. 

But one fair warning. If you have Arachnophobia, I wouldn’t recommend the game directly.  There are spiders and their nets everywhere. And you often have to walk through them. 
But you have a handy lighter and can burn them all down! I just wanted to mention that since you encounter this for most of the game.

Ah, [i]Metro[/i]. Part shooter—well, mostly shooter, of course, but it also has strong elements of survival/resource management, and, oddly enough, walking simulator. Yes, you heard me right: there are decent chunks of the game where you just get to walk, soak in the atmosphere, listen to characters' conversations, amd do extremely important things like burning spider web. The tense gameplay sections are thus interspersed with almost completely non-interactive mood-pieces, making for a nice pace.

The shooting feels good, with different weapons being sufficiently different and allowing for various strategies. The resource management is not especially hard on non-Ranger difficulties. It does try hard to ramp tension up with its famously diegetic interfaces, your face mask getting dirty and obcsuring your vision and so on, but that doesn't really work if you keep in mind that it's just cosmetics. Moreover, the sections between checkpoints aren't especially gruelling, so dying isn't that scary anyway, since your progress isn't terribly hard to retrace. (That lead me to a funny dynamic where I would die deliberately and restart a section if I was too short of supplies, because finishing a section in a bad state is worse than replaying it.)

The game's tone is curious. It takes itself extremely seriously and plays each trope with a face so straight, I think its jaw might break. It's honestly unclear if it realises that some of its more absurd scenes, like a station locked in a perpetual war between fascists and communists, are farcical and hilarious. And the game's all-too-serious machismo is very funny sometimes.

But I guess that's the price we get to pay for the incredible beauty of a collapsed Moscow and its underground in all its morose half-ruined glory. With the Redux edition, almost every scene and section is a sight to behold, with gritty art direction and great mood filling in the gaps wherever the visuals themselves look slightly outdated. (Although, honestly, the game looks great even today.) While I wouldn't say I became very interested in characters' stories, because they were all a bit too similar and died a bit too often, I was absolutely enthralled with places, be they unfriendly open vistas where you grasp for breathable air or intertwining underground tunnels with abandoned side passages.

One minor gripe I have with the game is that when it does for some reason offer you a "story" choice, it's handled poorly. Yes, it was glaringly obvious that the whore inviting me in was a trap, but the only way to avoid it was non-participation, and what player will just skip content voluntarily? You're no [i]STALKER[/i], [i]Metro[/i], and you don't need to be; you're linear and good at what you do, so leave that immersive stuff for other games.

I like [i]Metro[/i] for what it is: for its incredible atmosphere, nice shooting and level design offering different approaches to situations, and for how oddly relaxed and slow it can be for a survival/shooter. And I think it still fully holds up today.

Metro 2033 Redux, developed by 4A Games and released in 2014, is a remastered version of the original game from 2010, based on the novel of the same name by Dmitry Glukhovsky. It’s a first-person shooter blending exploration, survival, and horror, set in a post-apocalyptic universe reminiscent of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and Fallout, but with an added layer of intense claustrophobia.

The story unfolds in 2033, in a Russia devastated by nuclear war. Survivors have taken refuge in Moscow’s metro system, connected by dark, grim tunnels, with each station governed by factions with wildly differing ideologies. You play as Artyom, a young man from the VDNKh station, tasked with warning the inhabitants of Polis station about an imminent supernatural threat. You’ll need to navigate from station to station to help as many people as possible, while avoiding numerous dangers, including supernatural events, countless mutants, or soldiers from hostile factions.

Danger and horror permeate the metro’s tunnels, where everything is grim, cramped, dark, oppressive, and toxic. Yet, these passages are essential, linking the various stations. Many factions have set up their bases here, such as the Reds, the Reich, or various bandit groups.

Some stations, fortunately, house friendly, almost warm communities despite the dire circumstances. Life goes on, offering a glimpse of near-normalcy among their inhabitants. People chat, joke, barter, listen to music, raise animals, cook, eat, and children draw. You can take the opportunity to buy essentials for survival, like gas masks, filters, medkits, ammunition, weapons, and upgrades. These underground cities provide a chance to warm your heart and spirit, and stock up on gear before heading back into the tunnels, moving "station to station", as David Bowie might say.

As for the surface, prepare to discover the eerie charm of a post-apocalyptic Moscow. The surface is even more hostile than the underground, with unbreathable air, abandoned and ruined landscapes, and bone-chilling cold, if not worse. Be cautious—mutants now rule this domain!

You’ll face a variety of mutants everywhere, as well as soldiers from factions with questionable ideologies. But you don’t always have to charge in guns blazing—stealth is an option. With enough composure, you can sneak through hostile territory, disable traps, turn off lights, and silently take out or knock out enemies.

Boasting exceptional storytelling, enhanced by stunning, highly detailed graphics and a beautiful orchestral soundtrack, Metro 2033 Redux is a magnificent, cinematic, narrative, and dramatic experience. The game sets the bar high in every aspect—play it without hesitation!

Metro 2033 Redux is a post-apocalyptic story-rich first person shooter developed by 4A Games and published by Deep Silver. This title takes place in Moscow some 20 years following a nuclear holocaust that has destroyed the world that we know and forced what was left of mankind to seek shelter in the underground Metro stations scattered throughout Russia. Over that time humanity has formed a new civilization in these tunnels and managed to survive...for the most part. You take on the role of Artyom, a young man on a quest to save his home station, the Exhibition, from being overrun by hostile mutants. Artyom's intriguing journey will take him on a terrifying excursion through the dark monster and bandit infested tunnels of the Metro station as well as above ground into the irradiated remnants of the devastated world above as he desperately tries to save his people.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1] 

At it's heart Metro 2033 Redux is a first person shooter wrapped around a very deep narrative driven story. As a shooter, I really enjoyed the gunplay in this wonderfully developed title. The weapons responded well and each felt different so you'll definitely have alot of fun experimenting with them until you find the loadout that suits your particular playstyle. There are an abundance of interesting weapons ranging from shotguns and assault rifles to pistols and throwing knives each with a number of attachments to add if you should choose to upgrade your arsenal. Gunstocks, extended cartridges, scopes and many other choices are at your disposal if you happen to pick them up during your adventures or purchase them from a vendor. In my opinion, one of the best things about Metro's gameplay is the ability to complete your missions in multiple ways. You could choose to go in guns blazing or you may have the option to try stealth and take out the enemy from the shadows or just avoid combat altogether if one so chooses. Yet another strength of this amazing game is the highly intriguing storyline and post-apocalyptic lore of the Metro franchise as well as the bonus of experiencing this facet of European culture. 

[h1]VISUALS[/h1]

This title showcases some of the most impressive visuals that I've seen in a first person shooter all brought to you in a completely immersive and highly cinematic fashion. For years I'd been hearing just how immersive the Metro titles were and now after having played them I totally agree with that assessment. Metro 2033 Redux does an exceptional job of taking intense gameplay with narrative enhancing cutscenes, action packed quick time events and seamlessly blending them together for a truly extraordinary gameplay experience. Add to that the beautiful high resolution textures, fantastic lighting, terrific special effects like depth of field among many others and the visual presentation of the title soars above most other games in the F.P.S. genre. Oh and don't forget that these impressive visuals are wrapped around a very intriguing post apocalyptic story-rich narrative which is always enjoyable in my opinion. Simply put, Metro 2033 Redux is a gorgeous game which makes the experience that much more enjoyable alongside the excellent storyline.

[h1]CONCLUSION[/h1]

After having just completed this title for the first time all I can say is wow what a ride! This was a fantastic introduction into the world and lore of the Metro franchise. I really look forward to playing the other games and reading the books as well because this series has really captured my attention. Replayability is high as there are some vital choices throughout the narrative that Artyom will have to make that could affect events and the games ending and there's also a number of achievements to acquire as well. The only downside to this title for me was that it was quite short as I completed it in about 15 hours. Since I like to explore and look for loot I'm quite sure other, more focused, players could finish the game in 11-13 hours. 

Also, I did run into a few technical problems as the game crashed on me but only once and additionally I had to restart some areas due to the N.P.C.'s being stuck in frozen positions and not moving although it did make them easier targets to take down haha! As far as options go, there are a number of Steam Achievements to hunt down and Steam Trading Cards to collect. Also available are the Spartan, Survivor and for the hardcore enthusiasts the Ranger modes of play. In conclusion, I think this title really manages to stand apart from the typical F.P.S. games due to the immersive gameplay and add to that the bleakness of the world, very interesting story and Metro 2033 Redux is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to post-apocalyptic, story-rich shooter fans one and all.

Originally released back in 2010, Metro 2033 is based on Dmitry Glukhovsky's novel turned video game by small studio, 4A Games and was highly praised for its atmospheric setting and compelling experience. At initial release, the game was such a resource hog that demanded more than Crysis in terms of performance. Fast forward to 2014 and we have the Redux version improving upon the game with better graphics, stability and more streamlined mechanics.

Post-nuclear war, survivors were forced to take shelter down below the metro tunnels of Russia. Going up to the surface was mostly feared upon and with reason. I quickly dreaded the time I had to get out and progress the game. With such high levels of radiation outside the tunnels, I frequently needed to change out my gas mask filter in order to survive. And these filters didn't come in handy, neither did bullets. Stealth here was my friend and made for a better experience. Metro stations were my safe haven. Finally, It was a place to breathe fresh air and stock up on supplies. It was a nice place short lived by the horrors I had to face.

I went in with an open mind and was impressed. I certainly didn't mind the linear approach when everything else worked so well. There’s something magnetically terrible about The Metro. It has dark and enclosed tunnels. The lack of quality weaponry. The even lower ammunition. It’s set in a dilapidated and decrepit environment, where the goal is simply to survive. There’s this pervasive feeling of uneasiness that lingers no matter how still the environment is. I’ve literally spent hours just walking the tunnels and listening to people and, believe it or not, some of those moments without even conflict were more memorable than some of the actual confrontations.

The Metro doesn’t reshape the world to make it happier and easier. You won’t be the world savior. Bringing you back to the lonely emptiness of the world, it brings you into a personal space that I think a lot of people enjoy; the presence of people, but knowing you’re on your own.

This isn’t the most hand-polished and well put together game, but I’d take this over a hundred more open world games who try to fit as many crosshairs and icons to collect into a world all for themselves.

All you really need is a dark tunnel, a few ammo rounds, and that awful feeling that you really shouldn’t be traveling that tunnel.

It is safe to say that, due to the structural complexity, game projects do not exist without any flaws. However, one of the main differences between a good game and a mediocre one is a sincere desire to forgive these very mistakes and weak points. And an example of this is Metro 2033 - a noteworthy shooter with an incredibly dark post-apocalyptic atmosphere, a very strong plot with light notes of mysticism and a philosophical message, hot battles with not very smart, but hardy opponents, as well as a rather specific sense of shooting and a kind of stealth. The game universe turned out to be frighteningly realistic, and the design of the locations played an important role in this. Catacombs shrouded in darkness, the remains of a former civilization, decayed or still fresh corpses, an ominous howl and eerie growling of hungry monsters - an extremely gloomy picture that makes you feel genuine anxiety and constant moral discomfort. Fortunately, some semblance of society has survived in the station cities, but even there, looking at the shacks of the inhabitants, a feeling of hopelessness arises. Dozens of accidentally spied scenes and dialogues taken straight from the book immerse you even deeper. Music was also appropriate. Melancholic ambient and sad guitar chords are the final touches, naturally complementing the already sad image of widespread devastation and absolute despair. As for the Redux version, the creators made a lot of changes to the original and turned it into a big first chapter of a whole adventure (trilogy). It should be noted the updated character models, a completely changed lighting system, improved animation of the main character's movements and more adequate stealth mechanics. This game is not a revolution in the genre and does not stand out for any exclusivity, but this is not required of it. Among shooters with an interesting world and an outstanding concept, she already performs very well. It would be fair to put 9/10 - a small addition for a certain soulfulness, especially understandable for a Russian person, which allows Metro 2033 to be perceived as an okay and even unique work made in the post-Soviet space according to world standards.

I wasn't initially excited to play this game because it seemed to be too serious and intense. The atmosphere is dark and scary, especially at the Ghosts level. The game's field of view was too close for me, so I had to set it farther to make it less nauseating. Aim assist was also annoying so I had to turn it off because sometimes it would shoot anything besides your target. Both options weren't available in-game so I had to edit the game's config file manually.

The game has a good amount of weapon varieties. My go-to weapons would be anything that didn't have an absurd recoil. The enemy varieties, on the other hand, were mostly the same on most mission. The two most common ones were human enemies and the mutant, Nosalis. There are other mutants in the game, but they were only shown on a few occasions. Playing stealthily would be best until the last few stages of the game (at around the Church level).

The game is relatively simple and mostly the same because of how linear it is. I was able to finish my second playthrough relatively faster than my first one because I already knew what I was doing. I was skipping most loot and collectibles so that I could get my two final achievements which had something to do with the ending and what game mode you were playing (Survival or Spartan).

Overall, this game was an amazing experience. Even though the non-playable characters' faces are lifeless, the story is captivating enough to get your attention. I would recommend this to anyone who likes story-driven shooter games.

One of my top picked games - If you like a good story FPS with good lore and amazing atmosphere this is the game for you. 

I also encourage you to checkout the books
